# Story 09 — Advanced Ticket Management & Agent Workspace (Story: 09)

## Prerequisites

- Stories 01–08 completed and merged into `main` (auth, RBAC, audit logging, Customer CRUD, Ticket CRUD with Status + Assignment). This story extends — and must not break — those surfaces.
- No prior plans exist under `.squad/plans/`; this is the first plan file for the `advanced-ticket-management` feature slug. Follow the pattern established by the code in `TicketsController.cs`/`CustomersController.cs` (allow-list constants, `AuditLogger.WriteAsync`, `[Authorize]` on the class, `[Authorize(Roles = "Admin")]` only on Delete), and the frontend pattern established by `TicketsPage.tsx` / `CustomersPage.tsx` (list + modal, `useAuthStore`, `useTranslation`, EN/AR keys, logical Tailwind classes).

---

## Story Goal

Turn the existing Ticket surface into a real per-ticket "agent workspace" and add a per-customer detail view, without touching SLA/notifications/KB/portal/channels/reports/AI/multi-tenancy (Stories 10–14).

Concretely, this story delivers **12 audited capabilities as a single coordinated change**:

1. Ticket categories (server-validated `Category`).
2. Ticket priorities (server-validated `Priority`).
3. Per-ticket history (reuses `AuditLog`).
4. Per-customer interaction history (reuses `AuditLog`).
5. Ticket notes = team-collaboration thread (`TicketNote`).
6. Ticket attachments stored inline in SQL Server (`TicketAttachment`, 5 MB cap).
7. Ticket tasks / reminders unified into one entity (`TicketTask`).
8. "My tickets" client-side toggle on the Tickets list.
9. Ticket Detail page `/tickets/:id` — the agent workspace.
10. Customer Detail page `/customers/:id`.
11. Quick reply templates (`QuickReplyTemplate`) piped into the note composer.
12. `GET /api/tickets?customerId=` for the Customer Detail page's ticket list.

**Explicitly not in scope** (deferred, do not implement): SLA rules, alerts/notifications, auto-assignment, escalation, Knowledge Base, Customer Portal, email/SMS/WhatsApp/live chat, reports, AI features, admin UI for users/roles, multi-department/multi-branch/branding, generic search/sort/pagination, field-level audit diffs, polymorphic notes/attachments.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Category allow-list:** `General`, `Billing`, `Technical`, `Account`. Default `General` for existing rows and for new tickets without an explicit value.
- **Priority allow-list:** `Low`, `Normal`, `High`, `Urgent`. Default `Normal` for existing rows and for new tickets without an explicit value.
- **Notes AND team collaboration are the same thread.** No separate "chat" entity. Everyone with ticket access (`[Authorize]`, Admin + Agent) can read and post.
- **Attachments** are stored as `varbinary(max)` on `TicketAttachment`. Cap: **5 MB per file, enforced server-side.** No client-side filtering beyond a friendly reject.
- **Tasks AND reminders are the same entity.** `DueAtUtc` is nullable. UI highlights `IsDone = false && DueAtUtc <= now` in red, `DueAtUtc == today` in amber. **No push, no email, no notification.**
- **Quick replies** are shared, org-wide templates (`Title`, `Body`); any Admin or Agent may create/edit/delete (low-risk shared content — matches the intake's explicit direction).
- **Per-ticket history and per-customer history** are action narratives sourced from `AuditLogs`, not field-diffs.
- **My-tickets toggle** is client-only — filters the already-fetched list by `assignedToUserId === currentUserId`.
- **Audit-log write posture:** continue to audit only `customer.create/update/delete` and `ticket.create/update/delete`. Do **not** add audit entries for note/task/attachment/quick-reply sub-resource CRUD — that would inflate the new `/history` output and duplicate the parent update audit (which fires whenever the ticket itself changes).

```csharp
[HttpGet]
public async Task<IActionResult> List([FromServices] AppDbContext db, [FromQuery] Guid? customerId = null)
{
    var query = db.Tickets.AsQueryable();
    if (customerId.HasValue) query = query.Where(t => t.CustomerId == customerId.Value);
    var items = await query
        .OrderByDescending(t => t.CreatedAtUtc)
        .Select(/* extended TicketListItem projection */)
        .ToListAsync();
    return Ok(items);
}
```

Add — after the existing `Delete` action — the new sub-resource actions on `TicketsController` (keep them in the same file to match Stories 06–08's "one controller per top-level resource" style):

- `GET /api/tickets/{id:guid}/history` → `[Authorize]`
  Load `AuditLogs` where `Action.StartsWith("ticket.") && Details == id.ToString()`, join to `Users` for `ActorDisplayName`, order by `TimestampUtc`, project to `HistoryEntry`. Return 404 if the ticket does not exist.

- `GET /api/tickets/{id:guid}/notes` → `[Authorize]` — list notes joined with author display name, ordered by `CreatedAtUtc`.
- `POST /api/tickets/{id:guid}/notes` → `[Authorize]` — validate 404 for the ticket, `BadRequest("body_required")` if `string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(request.Body)`. `AuthorUserId = GetActorUserId()!.Value` (return 401 if null, matching `AuthController`'s stance). Return the newly created `TicketNoteItem` from `CreatedAtAction`. **Do not audit-log.**

- `GET /api/tickets/{id:guid}/attachments` → list metadata (never bytes).
- `POST /api/tickets/{id:guid}/attachments` → `[Authorize]`, accepts `IFormFile file` (multipart/form-data). Reject with 400 `file_required` if null, `file_too_large` if `file.Length > 5 * 1024 * 1024`. Read `await file.CopyToAsync(memoryStream)`. Store `FileName = Path.GetFileName(file.FileName)`, `ContentType = file.ContentType`, `SizeBytes = file.Length`, `Content = memoryStream.ToArray()`, `UploadedByUserId = GetActorUserId()!.Value`. Return `TicketAttachmentItem`.
- `GET /api/tickets/{id:guid}/attachments/{attachmentId:guid}/download` → `[Authorize]`. Load only the matching attachment (verify `TicketId == id`), return `File(a.Content, a.ContentType, a.FileName)`.
- `DELETE /api/tickets/{id:guid}/attachments/{attachmentId:guid}` → `[Authorize]` (matches ticket-update permission per intake — not Admin-only).

- `GET /api/tickets/{id:guid}/tasks` → list ordered `IsDone` asc, `DueAtUtc` asc-nulls-last, `CreatedAtUtc` asc.
- `POST /api/tickets/{id:guid}/tasks` → validate 404 for ticket, `BadRequest("title_required")` if blank.
- `PUT /api/tickets/{id:guid}/tasks/{taskId:guid}` → same validation. Verify `taskId` belongs to `id`.
- `DELETE /api/tickets/{id:guid}/tasks/{taskId:guid}`.

All new endpoints reuse `GetActorUserId()` for `AuthorUserId`/`UploadedByUserId` but **do not** call `AuditLogger.WriteAsync` (see "Product rules").

### 6 — `CustomersController` — customer history endpoint

**File: `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Controllers/CustomersController.cs`**

Add at the bottom of the class:

```csharp
[HttpGet("{id:guid}/history")]
public async Task<IActionResult> History(Guid id, [FromServices] AppDbContext db)
{
    var customer = await db.Customers.AnyAsync(c => c.Id == id);
    if (!customer) return NotFound(new { error = "customer_not_found" });

    var idStr = id.ToString();
    var items = await db.AuditLogs
        .Where(a => a.Action.StartsWith("customer.") && a.Details == idStr)
        .OrderBy(a => a.TimestampUtc)
        .Select(a => new HistoryEntry(a.Id, a.Action, a.Outcome, a.ActorUserId,
            a.ActorUserId == null ? null : db.Users.Where(u => u.Id == a.ActorUserId).Select(u => u.DisplayName).FirstOrDefault(),
            a.TimestampUtc))
        .ToListAsync();
    return Ok(items);
}
```

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Existing tickets after migration** — Category/Priority backfill to `"General"`/`"Normal"` via the migration's `defaultValue`. If the migration is deployed before the API is upgraded, EF will read the columns fine (they carry data). If the API is upgraded before the migration, requests will fail with SQL errors on missing columns; document "run `dotnet ef database update` before rolling the API" in the Migration section.
- **Attachment > 5 MB** — server rejects `file_too_large` with 400; the frontend shows `ticketDetail.attachments.tooLarge` and does not upload. Enforced in `TicketsController` new upload action.
- **Empty ticket / not-found ticket for sub-resources** — every new endpoint validates the ticket exists and returns 404 `ticket_not_found` (mirrors `TicketsController.cs:66`).
- **Deleting a ticket that has notes/attachments/tasks** — FKs cascade (see fluent config in step 2). No leftover rows; audit log entries are preserved (audit logs are not FK'd to Tickets).
- **Deleting a user who authored notes/attachments/uploaded quick-replies** — FK is `Restrict`; delete fails at the DB layer. Since Story 04 does not currently support user deletion in the UI, this is acceptable; document as a known constraint.
- **My-tickets toggle for an unauthenticated user** — impossible in practice because `/tickets` is behind `RequireAuth`, but guard `visibleTickets = userId ? … : tickets` anyway.
- **Persisted auth state missing `id` after upgrade** — handled by the Zustand persist version bump (drops old session so user re-logs in). Documented in `useAuthStore.ts`.
- **Category / Priority typed with wrong case** — 400 `category_invalid` / `priority_invalid`; frontend `<select>` fields prevent this in normal flow.
- **`?customerId=<not-a-guid>`** — ASP.NET model binding returns 400 automatically for invalid Guid, matching `[HttpGet("{id:guid}")]` behaviour elsewhere.
- **Quick reply picker with zero templates** — the `<select>` shows a placeholder option only; no error.
- **Task due date in the past on create** — allowed (agent may retroactively log a due date). UI highlights it as overdue immediately.
- **RTL rendering of the new Ticket/Customer detail pages** — use `ps-*`/`pe-*`/`start-*`/`end-*` per the established Tailwind convention. Do not use `pl-*`/`pr-*`/`left-*`/`right-*`.
- **Arabic strings in note bodies / attachment filenames** — stored as-is (Unicode-safe via EF Core + SQL Server `nvarchar`/`varbinary(max)`).
- **Multiple agents editing the same note thread concurrently** — no locking; last-write-wins on notes composer; both writes appear as separate entries because notes are append-only.

## Migration / Rollback

- **Deployment order:** deploy the migration (`dotnet ef database update`) **before** the API. The added `Category`/`Priority` columns are NOT NULL with defaults, so existing rows backfill safely. New tables are additive.
- **Rollback:** `dotnet ef database update <PreviousMigration>` reverses the migration. `LoginResponse.Id` is additive positional-record change; older clients that ignore it will still work. `AuthUser.id` on the frontend is optional-guarded so a stale bundle without it will still log in but the My-tickets toggle will be effectively no-op.
- **Half-applied risk:** if the API is upgraded before the migration runs, ticket queries fail with "invalid column name Category". Mitigate via the deploy-order rule.

1. **Backend builds:** in `backend/`, `dotnet build`. Confirm zero errors, zero new warnings.
2. **Backend migration:** in `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/`, `dotnet ef migrations add AddAgentWorkspace` (already done during implementation); then `dotnet ef database update`. Verify new tables exist in the local SQL Server via any query tool.
3. **Backend runs:** `dotnet run` in `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/`; call the smoke-test cURLs from the Test Plan.
4. **Frontend installs:** in `frontend/`, `npm install` (no new packages should have been added — check `package.json` diff is empty).
5. **Frontend lints:** `npm run lint` (or the existing script — grep `frontend/package.json` for `lint`). Zero errors.
6. **Frontend builds:** `npm run build`. Zero errors.
7. **Frontend runs:** `npm run dev`; walk through the UI smoke tests (10–14 above).
8. **Regression:** log in as Admin, then as Agent; exercise Story 07/08's existing quick-edit modal, status change, and assignment; check audit log is untouched by note/task/attachment activity.
